name: Sidebar
description: Navigates through a collapsible desktop rail that becomes a modal panel on smaller screens.

children.description: Sidebar content (use Sidebar.Header, Sidebar.Nav, Sidebar.Section, etc.)

collapsed.description: Desktop: the rail is collapsed (controlled). Ignored inside a Sidebar.Provider or AppShell.

collapsible.description: How the rail collapses: to its glyphs (icon), off the canvas (offcanvas), or never (none)

aria-label.description: Accessible label for the rail and the mobile panel

when: Primary navigation for an app shell
Navigation that must collapse to icons or hide entirely
whenNot: Temporary side panels for one task (use Drawer)
guidelines: Give every item an icon so the collapsed rail stays readable; with no glyphs, collapsing hides the rail
collapsible="icon" shrinks to the glyph rail; "offcanvas" takes it off the canvas, and Header.Trigger brings it back
Sidebar.Header shows collapsedContent alone while the rail is collapsed; give it the brand mark so a full brand never clips
Set state on Sidebar when it stands alone; wrap in Sidebar.Provider (or AppShell) when a header trigger or other code must drive it, and set state there
The current item takes the neutral current fill and ink 1 at the regular weight, with no ring; mark it with active
Sidebar.Item and Sidebar.SubItem take render for router links
Sidebar rows also work outside a Sidebar, for example in a Drawer for a header's mobile navigation
Use Sidebar.MenuSkeleton inside a Section while navigation data loads
accessibility: The rail is a labelled <aside>; Sidebar.Nav is a labelled <nav>
aria-expanded on items with submenus and on collapsible section labels
Below md the panel is a modal dialog: focus trap, a visible close, Escape closes, the scrim closes
Collapsed rows keep their label for assistive tech and show it in a tooltip
Rows are at least 32px tall (the md control track) and the section action has a 32px hit area; under a coarse pointer both reach the 44px hit-area floor

examples.name: Default
examples.description: A rail with sections, the current item and a collapse toggle.
examples.code:
import { House as HouseIcon, ListBullets as ListIcon } from "@phosphor-icons/react";
import { Sidebar } from '@/components/Sidebar';

<Sidebar>
  <Sidebar.Header>Workspace</Sidebar.Header>
  <Sidebar.Nav>
    <Sidebar.Section label="Workspace">
      <Sidebar.Item icon={<HouseIcon />} href="/overview" active>Overview</Sidebar.Item>
      <Sidebar.Item icon={<ListIcon />} href="/findings">Findings</Sidebar.Item>
    </Sidebar.Section>
  </Sidebar.Nav>
  <Sidebar.Footer>
    <Sidebar.CollapseToggle />
  </Sidebar.Footer>
</Sidebar>

examples.name: Row States
examples.description: Badges, a working row and a disabled row.
examples.code:

      <Sidebar.Item icon={<GearIcon />} working>Setup</Sidebar.Item>
      <Sidebar.Item icon={<ChartIcon />} disabled>Adoption</Sidebar.Item>
    </Sidebar.Section>
  </Sidebar.Nav>
</Sidebar>

examples.name: With Submenu
examples.description: A row opens a nested list.
examples.code:
import { Gear as GearIcon } from "@phosphor-icons/react";
import { Sidebar } from '@/components/Sidebar';

<Sidebar>
  <Sidebar.Nav>
    <Sidebar.Section>
      <Sidebar.Item icon={<GearIcon />} hasSubmenu defaultExpanded>Settings</Sidebar.Item>
      <Sidebar.Submenu>
        <Sidebar.SubItem href="/settings/general" active>General</Sidebar.SubItem>
        <Sidebar.SubItem href="/settings/members">Members</Sidebar.SubItem>
      </Sidebar.Submenu>
    </Sidebar.Section>
  </Sidebar.Nav>
</Sidebar>

examples.name: With Provider & Header Trigger
examples.description: Sidebar.Provider holds the state so Header.Trigger can open the mobile panel.
examples.code:
import { House as HouseIcon } from "@phosphor-icons/react";
import { Header } from '@/components/Header';
import { Sidebar } from '@/components/Sidebar';

<Sidebar.Provider collapsible="offcanvas">
  <Header>
    <Header.Trigger />
    <Header.Brand href="/">Workspace</Header.Brand>
  </Header>
  <Sidebar>
    <Sidebar.Nav>
      <Sidebar.Section>
        <Sidebar.Item icon={<HouseIcon />} active>Overview</Sidebar.Item>
      </Sidebar.Section>
    </Sidebar.Nav>
    <Sidebar.Footer>
      <Sidebar.CollapseToggle />
    </Sidebar.Footer>
  </Sidebar>
</Sidebar.Provider>

examples.name: Router Links
examples.description: render moves the row's look and props onto a router link.

examples.name: With Section Action
examples.description: A collapsible section with one action beside its label.
examples.code:
import { Plus as PlusIcon, Folder as RepoIcon } from "@phosphor-icons/react";
import { Sidebar } from '@/components/Sidebar';

<Sidebar>
  <Sidebar.Nav>
    <Sidebar.Section
      label="Repositories"
      collapsible
      action={<Sidebar.SectionAction aria-label="Add repository"><PlusIcon /></Sidebar.SectionAction>}
    >
      <Sidebar.Item icon={<RepoIcon />}>web</Sidebar.Item>
    </Sidebar.Section>
  </Sidebar.Nav>
</Sidebar>

relations.note: AppShell.Sidebar wraps Sidebar and holds its state
Header.Trigger opens the mobile panel and brings back a hidden rail
Sidebar rows in a Drawer give a header-only app its mobile navigation
Use Menu for contextual actions within the sidebar

propsSummary: collapsed / defaultCollapsed / onCollapsedChange - the desktop rail
open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange - the mobile panel
Sidebar.Provider holds the state when something outside the rail drives it
useSidebar() - state and toggleSidebar; inert defaults outside a sidebar
